holidays.name: Cellophane Tape Day
holidays.description: Salute the humble sticky strip that holds gifts, torn pages, and half your household together. Today is the day to appreciate the clear tape you can never find the end of.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that honors the invention of clear cellophane tape. 3M engineer Richard Drew developed it in the early 1930s, after he had first created masking tape for auto painters.
holidays.funFact: The 'Scotch' in Scotch tape started as an insult. An irritated auto painter called the early tape stingy because the adhesive only ran along the edges, and the name stuck.

holidays.name: National Grape Popsicle Day
holidays.description: Celebrate the purple, tongue-staining frozen treat of summer. Grab one and see who in the room ends up with the most colorful smile.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors the grape flavor of the frozen pop, a classic that has cooled off kids for generations.
holidays.funFact: The Popsicle was reportedly invented by accident in 1905. An 11-year-old named Frank Epperson left a cup of soda powder and water with a stirring stick outside on a freezing night.

holidays.name: National Gray Day
holidays.description: Embrace the most underrated color on the palette. Wear gray, admire gray skies, and celebrate everything between black and white.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It gives a little love to a shade that often gets dismissed as dull.
holidays.funFact: Many languages treat gray as a mood as much as a color. English even has two spellings, 'gray' and 'grey', and both are correct.
